short.en: Add a gate outside the part

t.en: In a mountain city, some crossings are blocked by fallen rocks (the hatched cells), and no route may pass through them.
The tray holds the <part-ref to="counter"></part-ref>: it adds up its “up” and “left” ports, plus 1 when its “start” port is “yes”.

This level’s This cell panel adds “is rock”, and the tray has a new component: the Block gate. It is the exact opposite of the Pass gate: when its condition is “yes” it outputs “—”; otherwise it lets the number through unchanged.
Think about it: how many routes from the start to a rock cell can actually be traveled? What should a rock cell output?

goal.en: Only right or down, and no route may pass through a rock cell (hatched). Have the robot count the routes correctly in cities with rockfalls too.

how.en: The Route Counter is in the tray, ready to go on the board.

body.en: Once a rock cell outputs “—”, every route through it is cut off: Mergers skip “—”, so it adds nothing to the cells after it.
Nothing inside the Route Counter had to change. You just added a gate outside it. A finished part can be used as it is, with a little something new added to handle a new situation.

note.en: A cell that can’t be passed outputs “—”, which rules out every route through it.

hints.en: Routes can’t pass through rocks. How many routes from the start can actually get to a rock cell?
Place a Route Counter and a Block gate: wire This cell’s “is rock” to the gate’s condition port and the Route Counter into its number port, then wire the Block gate to “this cell”.
